title: Tokenflow harmonizer: region fallback hotfix to stabilize TTFT and tokens/sec
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported a sudden TTFT regression and sustained tokens/sec throughput drop after a microkernel scheduling tweak deployed in runtime-1.22. The regression manifests as 2–3x higher TTFT for short-chat workloads and up to 60% drop in tokens/sec for multiplexed sessions on heterogeneous model mixes (large-decoder variants + quantized variants).

Scope: Affects multi-region Hosted endpoints with cross-region fallback enabled, Dedicated pools that share model variants across AZs, and Private deployments with hybrid routing enabled. Incident correlates with increased fanout to fallback model variants and asymmetric token draining when region-level prefetch budgets are exhausted.

Why this ticket: We need a targeted, deployable hotfix that (1) stabilizes TTFT for impacted customers within the next 48 hours, (2) prevents repeated fanout amplification during short spikes, and (3) provides observability and rollback criteria. This ticket captures investigation notes, a short-term patch (tokenflow harmonizer + region-fallback backoff), and follow-ups for longer-term kernel selection/eviction correctness.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a multi-tenant Hosted endpoint with model variants: redwood/llama2-70b-8bit, redwood/mistral-medium-quant, and a CPU-compatible reranker.
2) Enable cross-region fallback and set warmup=on and prefetch_budget=default.
3) From region A, flood the endpoint with short 16-token chat priming requests at tps=150 for 30s, then drop to 30 tps.
4) Observe first-token latency (TTFT) and aggregate tokens/sec on region B and the fallback pool for 5 minutes.
hypothesis: - The kernel scheduler change (kernel-multiplex-priority v2) biases eviction ordering when model variants have heterogeneous quantization, causing prefetch credits to be consumed asymmetrically across replicas.
- Cross-region fallback triggers additional fanout to compatible variants; without a backoff this multiplies outstanding warmups and stalls first-token paths for unrelated requests.
- Prefetch budget accounting lacks per-customer amortization, so one noisy tenant can starve tokensync lanes for others leading to tokens/sec collapse.
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): implement 'tokenflow harmonizer' middleware that introduces: (a) region-fallback exponential backoff for warmup-triggered fanout, (b) per-customer prefetch cap with soft-degradation threshold, and (c) immediate priority demotion for queued warmups when overall queueing latency exceeds 80th percentile SLA.

Deploy path: push hotfix to runtime-1.22 branch -> Canary in Hosted region us-east-1 with canary traffic pinned to 5% -> monitor for 30m -> promote to Dedicated staging pools -> schedule Private patch rollout via customer package.
Instrumentation: emit tokenflow.harmonizer.* metrics (backoff_applied, prefetch_capped, demotion_count) and a composite SLA metric tokenflow.stabilized_by_hotfix.
acceptance_criteria: - Canary: TTFT 95th-percentile decreases to within 15% of pre-incident baseline for short-chat workloads over a 1h sliding window.
- Canary: tokens/sec recovers to at least 85% of baseline for multiplexed sessions.
- No CPU/GPU utilization regression >5% after patch rollout in canary pools.
- All telemetry emitted and dashboard links verified.
monitoring: SLO alerts: paging on tokenflow.stabilized_by_hotfix == false for >15m
Canary checks: synthetic short-chat runner at https://ci.redwood.ai/synthetics/tokenflow-canary
